dct_description_sm: This project was designed to assist local community governments in measuring and adapting to the effects of climate change, as well as developing a coordinated response between various governments and First Nations organizations. The main objectives were in the first year: (1) to develop a plain language climate change planning poster and use it as an education tool during visits to communities to promote climate change planning; (2) to give climate change presentations to organizations that support community governments; (3) to support communities in upgrading and maintaining infrastructure in response to permafrost degradation; (4) to perform a preliminary risk assessment of climate change impacts on wastewater and water management systems in communities in the Northwest Territories (NWT); and (5) to support Tlicho climate change planning, as well as additional community and regional climate change planning in First Nation communities.   The second year aimed to develop a protocol for assessing the vulnerability of water and wastewater systems to climate change on a community-specific basis. The specific objectives of the project were: (1) to continue to support Tlicho climate change planning by conducting community-based and scientific/technical research and supporting the Tlicho Government in other duties; (2) to develop the protocol and use it to conduct pilot-scale assessments in three Northwest Territory communities; (3) to share conclusions and recommendations from Navigating the Waters of Change (a climate change impact document by Ecology North) with NWT community leaders; (4) to continue visiting the Northwest Territories communities to advocate climate change planning; and (5) to support additional regional and community climate change planning processes. The project continued work in the following year (2010-2011).   The project aimed to complete the following objectives in its third year: (1) To coordinate and support climate change adaptation planning and action plan implementation within four Northwest Territory communities (Behchok, Gameti, Wekweeti, and What);(2) to develop a planning toolkit to distribute throughout the Northwest Territories; and (3) to implement community-based water monitoring education and training in one community in the territory.
